LESSON: BREEDS OF LIVESTOCK ● CATTLE ● PIGS ● RABBITS ● SHEEP ● GOATS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: AGRICULTURE
Strand: Animal Production
Topic 2.1: Breeds of Livestock ● Cattle ● Pigs ● Rabbits ● Sheep ● Goats
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Breeds of Livestock ● Cattle ● Pigs ● Rabbits ● Sheep ● Goats, part of Animal Production in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 AGRICULTURE.

Key inquiry question: How do livestock breeds affect productivity of animals? 2. How does animal production sector contribute to the country’s economy?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. describe breeds of livestock based on their uses,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Breeds of Livestock ● Cattle ● Pigs ● Rabbits ● Sheep ● Goats in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. distinguish common breeds of livestock based on their characteristics,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Breeds of Livestock ● Cattle ● Pigs ● Rabbits ● Sheep ● Goats in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. analyse the contribution of animal production in the economy,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Breeds of Livestock ● Cattle ● Pigs ● Rabbits ● Sheep ● Goats in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate diversity of productivity from different livestock breeds. Learner is guided in purposive group, pair or individually to: ● use information from digital and print resources to describe breeds of cattle, pigs, rabbits, sheep and goats. Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech/ write/ type or use Augmentative and Alternative modes of 1. How do livestock breeds affect productivity of animals? 2. How does animal production sector contribute to the country’s economy? 26 Communication, AAC. Those with postural difficulties could be appropriately positioned to enhance access to the devices. Regulate glare on the digital devices screens for earners who are sensitive to light, ● take a field trip, excursion or observe resource media to distinguish common breeds of livestock based on their observable characteristics. Learners with mobility difficulties could use assistive technology for movement during the field trip. Communication, AAC, 27 ● discuss the role of animal production in the country’s economy, ● discuss and make presentations on comparative productivity from various livestock breeds. Core Competences to be developed: ● Digital literacy: learner connects digital devices when searching for information on common breeds of livestock. ● Communication and collaboration: learner displays teamwork by contributing ideas on characteristics of various breeds of livestock.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Breeds of Livestock ● Cattle ● Pigs ● Rabbits ● Sheep ● Goats together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Unity: learner appreciates the effort of others when discussing characteristics of various breeds of livestock.

● Respect: learner accommodates other’s ideas while discussing common breeds of livestock and their productivity.

28

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Financial literacy: learner appreciate the importance of investing in the animal production sector when discussing the

contribution of livestock in the country’s economy.

● Social economic and environmental issues: learner appreciate how different breeds of livestock maintain biodiversity in

our environment and its associated benefits.

● Social economic and environmental issues: learner appreciate safe road infrastructure by observing various classes of roads

(rural and urban) and their importance during a field trip or excursion to observe different breeds of livestock.

Suggested Learning Resources: Live animal breeds, photographs/ videos/ pictures of different livestock breeds, The pictures

and photographs should be of clear colour contrast and possibly mounted on cardboard or heavy gauge paper, Adapted computers

with appropriate accessibility features (large keyboards, trackballs, sticky keys, embedded touchpads), Appropriate applications

(text-to-speech conversion, speech recognition, eye-tracking for operations), Ergonomic and head-operated mouse and

footboards, Writing resources (padded pens pencils with enhanced grip, book holders and page turners, multipurpose stamps,

slant boards, theme-based multipurpose communication boards, Manilla papers/ heavy-gauge paper and marker pens/ adapted

marker pens, seats with worktops fixed to the side of the less affected arm hand, universal cuffs and typing aids),

Positioning devices (chest neck braces, prone wedges beds, special seats with straps, tables with adjustable heights and

inclination), ICT tools with appropriate accessibility features (cameras, projectors, radios, DVD and CD players, internet

connectivity), Other related services (physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, learner support)
